title: Horta & Schiavon (2025)
subtitle: Modelling the density and mass of the Milky Way's proto-galaxy components with APOGEE-Gaia
summary: This paper models the density and mass of the Milky Way's 'proto-galaxy' (centrally concentrated, metal-poor stars) using APOGEE-Gaia data, finding it follows a triaxial Plummer profile.

title: Han et al. (2022)
subtitle: The Stellar Halo of the Galaxy is Tilted and Doubly Broken
summary: This paper uses the H3 Survey to infer the shape and density profile of the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GSE) stellar halo, finding it is best described by a tilted triaxial ellipsoid with a doubly broken power law. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core to regularize the central density.

parameters.Model: Tilted Triaxial Doubly Broken Power Law

title: Amarante et al. (2024)
subtitle: Mapping the anisotropic Galactic stellar halo with blue horizontal branch stars
summary: This study uses blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars from Legacy Survey photometric data to map the stellar halo density. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core to regularize the central density.

title: Chen et al. (2023)
subtitle: Mapping the milky way’s stellar halo with 2D data
summary: This paper proposes a new method for measuring the spatial density distribution of the stellar halo using RR Lyrae stars. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core to regularize the central density.

title: Yang et al. (2022)
subtitle: Constructing the Milky Way Stellar Halo in the Galactic Center by Direct Orbit Integration
summary: This study integrates the orbits of ~10,000 LAMOST K giants to construct the stellar halo density at all radii. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core to regularize the central density.

title: Hernitschek et al. (2018)
subtitle: The Profile of the Galactic Halo from Pan-STARRS1 3π RR Lyrae
summary: This study uses Pan-STARRS1 RR Lyrae stars to map the stellar halo out to 150 kpc, finding it follows a broken power law with significant flattening in the inner regions. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Horta et al. (2021)
subtitle: The contribution of N-rich stars to the Galactic stellar halo using APOGEE red giants
summary: This study performs density modeling of both the general stellar halo and N-rich stars (dissolved globular cluster stars). This model version represents their triaxial disc cut-off (TRI-CUT-DISC) fit for the general halo field and includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Kurbatov et al. (2024)
subtitle: The realm of Aurora: Density distribution of metal-poor giants in the heart of the Galaxy
summary: This study maps the metal-poor 'Aurora' population in the inner Galaxy, finding it is highly concentrated and flattened. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Li & Binney (2022)
subtitle: Modelling the stellar halo with RR-Lyrae stars
summary: This study uses a distribution function approach to model RR Lyrae stars, revealing a smooth transition from a shallow inner halo to a steep outer halo. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: López-Corredoira et al. (2024)
subtitle: Stellar halo density with LAMOST K and M giants
summary: This study probes the outer halo using LAMOST giants, finding a spherical distribution and a steep power-law fall-off. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Lane et al. (2023)
subtitle: The stellar mass of the Gaia-Sausage/Enceladus accretion remnant
summary: This study uses the H3 Survey and APOGEE data to measure the density of the Gaia-Sausage/Enceladus (GSE) debris, finding a doubly-broken power-law profile with a prolate and tilted shape. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

parameters.Model: Prolate Tilted Doubly Broken Power Law

title: Lucey et al. (2026)
subtitle: Inferring Stellar Densities with Flexible Models. I. The Distribution of RR Lyrae in the Milky Way with Gaia DR3
summary: This study uses Gaia DR3 RR Lyrae stars to map the stellar halo, showing that the traditionally observed 'break' in the radial density profile may be explained by a transition in the halo's flattening. This model version follows their broken power-law fit and includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

parameters.Model: Single Power Law with Variable q

title: Mackereth & Bovy (2020)
subtitle: Weighing the stellar constituents of the galactic halo with APOGEE red giant stars
summary: This study uses APOGEE and Gaia data to characterize the stellar halo as a sum of individual populations. Their aggregate model follows a triaxial single power law with an exponential cut-off. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

parameters.Model: Triaxial Power Law with Exponential Cut-off

title: Medina et al. (2024)
subtitle: Taking the pulse of the outer Milky Way with HOWVAST: an RR Lyrae density profile out to >200 kpc
summary: This study extends the RR Lyrae density profile constraint out to >200 kpc, identifying a break at ~24 kpc. This model version follows their ellipsoidal broken power-law fit and includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Nibauer et al. (2025)
subtitle: Galactic Accelerations from the GD-1 Stream Suggest a Tilted Dark Matter Halo
summary: This study uses the GD-1 stellar stream to infer the Milky Way's acceleration field, finding evidence for a tilted and triaxial halo. This model version represents the associated stellar halo density and includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Stringer et al. (2021)
subtitle: Identifying RR Lyrae Variable Stars in Six Years of the Dark Energy Survey
summary: This study utilizes RR Lyrae variable stars from the Dark Energy Survey (DES) to map the stellar halo, finding a broken power-law profile with significant anisotropy. This model version follows their average radial fit and includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Suzuki et al. (2026)
subtitle: The Milky Way Tomography with Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam. II. Global halo structure
summary: This study uses Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam MSTO stars to map the stellar halo, finding a double power-law profile with a steep outer slope. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Wu et al. (2025)
subtitle: Mapping the Milky Way with Gaia Bp/Rp spectra: II. The inner stellar halo traced by a large sample of blue horizontal branch stars
summary: This study focuses on the inner stellar halo using BHB stars, emphasizing that the traditionally observed 'break' may be due to variable flattening. This model version follows their single power-law fit with variable flattening and includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Wu et al. (2022)
subtitle: Influence of the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus on the Density Shape of the Galactic Stellar Halo Revealed by Halo K Giants from the LAMOST Survey
summary: This study characterizes the stellar halo using K giant stars, finding a double power-law profile and highly variable flattening influenced by the GES merger debris. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Rix et al. (2022)
subtitle: The Poor Old Heart of the Milky Way
summary: This study identifies 'Aurora' as the ancient, metal-poor core of the Milky Way, formed before the Galactic disk. It follows a steep, nearly spherical density profile. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Cavieres et al. (2025)
subtitle: The Distant Milky Way Halo from the Southern Hemisphere: Characterization of the LMC-induced Dynamical Friction Wake
summary: This study uses photometric data from the Southern Hemisphere to map the distant stellar halo, identifying a triaxial broken power-law profile and the dynamical wake of the LMC. This model version follows their fit from section 5.2 and includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Feng et al. (2024)
subtitle: The Next Generation Virgo Cluster Survey. XXXVII. Distant RR Lyrae Stars and the Milky Way Stellar Halo Out to 300 kpc
summary: This study uses distant RR Lyrae stars from the NGVS to map the stellar halo, finding a smooth single power-law profile extending to 300 kpc. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Fukushima et al. (2025)
subtitle: Final results for mapping the Milky Way's stellar halo with blue horizontal branch stars selected from the Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam survey
summary: This study uses Subaru HSC BHB stars to map the outer stellar halo out to ~575 kpc, identifying a very steep drop-off in the extreme outer regions (splashback radius). This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Ye et al. (2023)
subtitle: Discovery of the shell structure via break radii in the outer halo of the Milky Way
summary: This study uses Gaia DR3 RR Lyrae stars to map the stellar halo density profile out to 120 kpc, identifying shell structures via density break radii. This model version follows their broken power-law fit and includes a 1 kpc constant density core.

title: Tao et al. (2026)
subtitle: The First Systematic Survey of Stellar Halos in High-inclination Galaxies
summary: This systematic census of 169 external galaxies finds that Milky Way-mass systems typically have extended stellar halos (~10% mass fraction), and that the Milky Way itself has an unusually quiescent merger history. This model represents a median external halo for comparison.

title: Medina et al. (2018)
subtitle: Discovery of Distant RR Lyrae Stars in the Milky Way Using DECam
summary: This study uses RR Lyrae stars from the HiTS survey to map the outer halo, finding a steep single power-law fit that extends to 200 kpc. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core.
